A Bloomberg report highlighted the remarkable returns Apple shareholders have enjoyed during Tim Cook's tenure as CEO. The cumulative gain reached 2,275%, and including dividends, the total return rate climbed even higher to 2,736%.

That report argued Cook has set a standard that will be tough to top. But I'd argue that incoming CEO John Ternus shouldn't try to replicate the Cook playbook...

The numbers Bloomberg cited are indisputable.

Still, I don't think Ternus needs to worry about whether Apple can match those financial results under his leadership. There are two reasons why.

First, both of his main predecessors believed financial success is a byproduct of the right goal, not something to chase directly. Steve Jobs famously said:

Cook himself echoed that sentiment, saying he never worried about quarterly results but focused on the company's longer-term direction.

Second, here's the advice Steve gave Tim when he took over:

Ternus shouldn't ask himself what Jobs or Cook would do. He should run Apple in whatever way he thinks is most likely to produce the best products, the best company culture and values, and long-term success.

I expect him to be a very different CEO from Cook, just as Cook was different from Jobs. The goal isn't to try to recreate the past winning formula but to look ahead and, to borrow a phrase from the outgoing CEO, follow your own north star.

Do you agree or disagree? Share your thoughts in the comments.
